item.title: Minimax designs and estimators for causal inference under network interference
item.description: arXiv:2611.08560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a design-based minimax theory for linear causal estimands under interference. We study the minimax risks of three problems: optimizing an estimator under a fixed design, optimizing an estimator and a design from a restricted class, or optimizing both over all designs. In each problem, we study the minimax risk over all estimators and over design-unbiased estimators separately. We allow any correctly specified exposure mapping, including the identity. Our theory represents causal inference under interference as a constrained sampling design on an expanded finite population of $\sum_i d_i$ potential outcomes, where $d_i$ is the number of exposure levels attainable by unit $i$. We describe the constrained sampling design by a weighted sampling hypergraph: its vertices are the potential outcomes, its hyperedges are the maximal sets of potential outcomes that can be jointly sampled under feasible treatment assignments, and its weights are induced by the randomization design. We show that the minimax risks of the fixed-design, restricted-design, and all-design problems depend, respectively, on the weighted hypergraph induced by the design, the collection of weighted hypergraphs attainable within the restricted class, and the unweighted hypergraph. Our Bayes lower bounds compare potential-outcome tables that differ on jointly missing sets of potential outcomes: joint-missingness probabilities govern the lower bounds over all estimators, whereas the corresponding odds govern the lower bounds over unbiased estimators. We illustrate the theory for average treatment effects without interference, saturation designs under partial interference, total, direct, and contagion effects under neighborhood interference, and bipartite dose-response contrasts. The upper and lower bounds match in several settings.
item.dc:creator: Vishesh Karwa, Edoardo M. Airoldi

item.title: An Asymptotic Framework for Closed-Form Estimators from Surrogate Estimating Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many statistical estimators, including maximum likelihood and method of moments estimators, are defined as roots of estimating equations. In complex models, these equations often cannot be solved explicitly; although numerical methods can provide approximate solutions, closed-form approximations can reduce computation and facilitate theoretical analysis by making an estimator's dependence on the data more transparent. In this paper, we develop a general approach to constructing such approximations and a framework for quantifying their accuracy. Our theory accommodates sequences of parameters that approach the boundary of the parameter space or diverge to infinity, and provides conditions under which a closed-form approximate estimator has the same first-order asymptotic distribution as its exact counterpart. We focus on approximations to maximum likelihood estimators, although the theory applies to general estimating equations. We apply the framework to iid models from the gamma, zeta, von Mises, and generalized Pareto families, as well as to gamma regression. Together, these examples cover scalar and vector parameters, iid and non-iid settings, and normal and nonnormal asymptotic regimes. Each example is accompanied by a simulation study, and the gamma regression example also includes a real-world data application.
item.dc:creator: Yigal Teplitsky, Robert Zimmerman

item.title: Exact optimality of augmented order-of-addition designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.
item.dc:creator: Stelios D. Georgiou, Haralambos Evangelaras, Stella Stylianou

item.title: Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+\tau^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $\tau$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($\tau^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $\tau$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.
item.dc:creator: Aoran Chen, Yang Feng

item.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.09087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.
item.dc:creator: Zhuohao Cheng

item.title: Byzantine-Robust Distributed Sparse Softmax Regression
item.description: arXiv:2611.09110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Byzantine-robust distributed sparse softmax regression in high-dimensional settings. We propose a communication-efficient distributed algorithm that employs robust aggregation methods---coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median---to defend against Byzantine attacks. Under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity constraints, we establish that the distributed estimator achieves the convergence rate of $O_{P}(K^{\frac{5}{2}}\sqrt{s\log(Kd)/N})$ when the Byzantine fraction $\alpha \asymp 1/\sqrt{m}$, matching the centralized oracle rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Wang, Yu Sun, Bowen Li, Kangqiang Li

item.title: Robust Bayes-like estimation of the distribution of a determinantal process
item.description: arXiv:2611.09426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the distribution of a determinantal process (DP) on a measured space from the observation of $n$ independent copies of it. Our estimator is obtained by sampling from a $T$-posterior distribution associated with a suitable prior, and we establish non-asymptotic risk bounds for the Hellinger loss which hold with high probability. These bounds remain valid when the data are only independent rather than i.i.d., and when the model is misspecified, which makes the estimator robust, for instance, to the presence of a small fraction of outliers. For determinantal projection processes of rank $k$ whose kernels are associated with $k$-dimensional subspaces of a $D$-dimensional space, Haar priors on Grassmannians lead to a rate of order $\sqrt{k(D-k)\log n/n}$, and model selection extends this result to infinite-dimensional settings. For general DPs, we introduce priors based on the spectral decomposition of the kernel that combine uniform distributions on the eigenvalues with Haar measures on Stiefel manifolds. When the underlying space is finite with $N$ elements, we obtain a rate of order $N\sqrt{\log n/n}$, without any assumption on the kernel, and derive that the $2^{N}$ principal minors of the kernel can be estimated simultaneously. Finally, for translation-invariant DPs on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, we obtain rates that only depend on the smoothness of the kernel at the origin and that are adaptive with respect to it. Combined with a new lower bound on the Hellinger distance between such DPs, these rates also yield estimators of the kernel in $\mathbb{L}_2$.
item.dc:creator: Yannick Baraud

item.title: On the Order of Privacy and Smoothing in Functional Mean Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential privacy (DP) is a leading framework for privacy protection, yet privacy mechanisms tailored to functional data analysis (FDA) remain relatively underexplored. For functional mean estimation, we investigate a fundamental question regarding the ordering of privatization and estimation by comparing two canonical pipelines: Fit-Then-Protect (FTP), which smooths trajectories before privatization, and Protect-Then-Fit (PTF), which privatizes observations at discrete time points before smoothing. When data are observed without error, we prove that FTP achieves strictly smaller mean squared error than PTF asymptotically (as the sample size increases) under the same $\mu$-Gaussian differential privacy ($\mu$-GDP) budget in both finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and infinite-dimensional reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). Simulation studies support our theory and explore settings with observation error and fitting constraints, demonstrating that FTP outperforms PTF under small observation noise, whereas PTF can become preferable in high-noise settings. In addition to this comparison, we establish a novel GDP guarantee for Gaussian perturbations taking values in a Banach space, extending existing results beyond the RKHS setting.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Chen, Yu-Wei Chen, Qifan Song, Jordan Awan

item.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
item.description: arXiv:2611.08784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Boris Landa, Francesco Strino, Fabio Parisi, Ruiqi Li, Yuval Kluger

item.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
item.description: arXiv:2611.08794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.
item.dc:creator: Saksham Jain, Guillaume Braun, Masaaki Imaizumi

item.title: Supervised Factor-Augmented Matrix Regression with Weak Factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.08941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a supervised factor-augmented matrix regression framework for high-dimensional analysis with weak factors. When factor loadings are concentrated on unknown subsets of rows and columns, conventional full-matrix factor extraction may suffer substantial signal dilution, with weakness in one matrix dimension propagating to estimation in the other. We characterize this two-way weak-loading phenomenon for both \(\alpha\)-PCA and projected estimators and show that their loading and factor estimates may deteriorate under weak signals. To address this problem, we propose a sequential response-guided screening procedure that identifies informative rows and columns prior to factor extraction. We establish exact support recovery and show that post-screening factor re-estimation converts the weak-loading problem into a pervasive one relative to the retained dimensions, yielding sharper convergence rates under substantially weaker dimensional growth conditions and consistent factor-number determination. We further establish asymptotic distributions for both unrestricted and bilinear regression estimators based on the estimated matrix factors. Simulations demonstrate substantial improvements in support recovery and factor estimation under weak signals. We illustrate the gains obtained by the response-guided factor construction with two empirical applications.
item.dc:creator: Wenyan Hou, Zhaoxing Gao, Ruey S. Tsay

item.title: M-Estimation in Censored Regression Model under Endogeneity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops a general M-estimation framework for censored regression models under endogeneity. A two-stage estimation is proposed to address the issue of endogeneity in the first stage and the issue of censoring in linear regression models in the second stage. The issue of endogeneity is addressed via instrumental variables using the control function approach. The issue of censoring in linear regression models is addressed via M-estimation using a suitably defined class of loss functions yielding a class of estimators. Thus, the proposed general M-estimation framework nests several existing estimators as special cases for the respective loss functions. Moreover, this provides flexibility of accommodating a broad range of robust loss functions that have not previously been studied in the context of censored regression. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed class of estimators. An empirical study based on simulated datasets is conducted to illustrate general M-estimation for various choices of loss functions and to examine the finite-sample performance of various resulting estimators.
item.dc:creator: Swati Shukla, Subhra Sankar Dhar, Shalabh

item.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.09592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Bani\'c, Neven Elezovi\'c

item.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, with a focus on how the regularity of the target should determine the choice of the kernel. We establish embeddings of analytic operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and derive finite-sample, high-probability guarantees that quantify the uncertainty due to random sampling: in the noiseless setting, suitable analytic kernels yield rates exponential in a fractional power of the sample size, while Sobolev-type kernels yield polynomial rates. We apply the theory to the solution operator of a parametric elliptic PDE, where the training data are themselves finite-element approximations, and obtain bounds that separate the sampling and discretization contributions to the error and prescribe how the mesh size should be coupled to the sample size. The results are illustrated numerically.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni S. Alberti, Markus Holzleitner, Lorenzo Rosasco, Matteo Santacesaria

item.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.
item.dc:creator: Jane Ivy Coons, Ben Hollering, Niharika Chakrabarty Paul

item.title: Limit laws for the friendship paradox in random geometric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The friendship paradox says that, on average, the neighbours of a vertex have more neighbours than the vertex itself. We study the size of this effect, the average over all vertices of the mean degree of the neighbours minus the degree of the vertex, in the random geometric graph on the torus with the maximum-norm distance. We determine its limit law in every regime of the connection radius and quantify the approximation by non-asymptotic error bounds in the Kolmogorov distance or the total variation distance. We also give its exact mean for every $n$ and every radius below one half. For a fixed radius the limit is not Gaussian but a weighted sum of centred exponential variables; when the radius shrinks and the expected degree grows, the statistic is asymptotically Gaussian, with a Berry--Esseen bound; for bounded expected degree it is Gaussian at the classical rate; and when the expected degree tends to zero it is asymptotically Gaussian, Poisson or identically zero, depending on how fast the radius shrinks. When the expected degree is large, the proofs rest on the vanishing of the first Hoeffding projection, which makes a degenerate $U$-statistic of pairs of points the source of the fluctuations; it is analysed by Fourier series for a fixed radius and by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs for a shrinking radius. For bounded expected degree we use normal approximation for local functionals, and for vanishing expected degree the Chen--Stein method.
item.dc:creator: Mingao Yuan

item.title: Box-Cox Transformations of Correlation Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.09790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider Box-Cox transformations of correlation matrices, $\Phi_\alpha(C)=\mathrm{vecl}\{(C^{\alpha}-I)/\alpha\}$, with Jacobian $J_\alpha$. The family nests the raw correlations at $\alpha=1$, the generalised Fisher transformation (GFT), $C\mapsto\mathrm{vecl}(\log C)$, at $\alpha=0$, and the negated off-diagonal concentration coordinates at $\alpha=-1$. The inverse problem is a strictly convex program for every $\alpha$, so every member is injective. The map is onto $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, $d=n(n-1)/2$, if and only if $\alpha\le0$, such that $\alpha=0$ defines the boundary for unrestricted parametrizations. For $\alpha>0$ the image is bounded. The conditioning obeys the bound $\kappa(J_\alpha)\le\kappa(C)^{|1-\alpha|}$, where $\kappa(C)=\lambda_{\max}(C)/\lambda_{\min}(C)$, and on the surjective range the exponent is smallest at $\alpha=0$. Under Gaussian sampling with $n\geq3$, the asymptotic covariance of the transformed sample correlations is the identity at independence for every member, but only $\alpha=0$ retains the identity to first order in the correlations, whereas the leading joint third cumulant at independence vanishes only at $\alpha=1/3$. Finally, applying the transformation to the diagonal rescaling of $C$ that makes the result hollow adds a new family to the existing correlation parametrizations. For every $\alpha$ the rescaling solves a strictly convex problem and the inverse is explicit, and the scaled coordinates are unrestricted exactly when $\alpha=0$, where they recover the known global normal coordinates, centred at independence, for the efficient information metric of the correlations.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Archakov, Peter Reinhard Hansen

item.title: Some ordering properties of highest and lowest order statistics with exponentiated Gumble type-II distributed components
item.description: arXiv:1904.08730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies stochastic comparisons of the highest and lowest order statistics arising from independent Exponentiated Gumbel Type-II distributed random variables. First, using vector majorization, we establish a comprehensive set of stochastic orderings for the lowest and highest order statistics with respect to the outer and inner shape parameters. In particular, for the lowest order statistic, we derive results on the usual stochastic order and likelihood ratio order, which further imply failure rate, mean residual life, and increasing convex orderings. Second, we show that the lowest order statistics satisfy a proportional failure rate structure. In addition, we also establish star and dispersive orderings. For the highest order statistic, we obtain results in the reversed failure rate order, and we show that, in general, a proportional failure rate structure does not hold. Moreover, unlike several classical exponentiated models, the highest order statistics are not necessarily comparable in the usual stochastic order under heterogeneity of the inner shape parameters. Finally, we extend the analysis using multivariate chain majorization to study the effect of simultaneous variation in scale and outer shape parameters. Under this framework, we establish usual stochastic ordering results for both the lowest and highest order statistics. It provides more general reliability comparisons under joint parameter heterogeneity.
item.dc:creator: Surojit Biswas

item.title: Functional Extreme-PLS
item.description: arXiv:2410.05517v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An extreme dimension reduction method is proposed, extending the Extreme-PLS approach to the discretized functional framework, where the covariate lies in the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space ($L^2([0,1])$) but is partially observed on a dense time grid. The ideas are partly borrowed from both Partial Least-Squares (PLS) and Sliced Inverse Regression (SIR) techniques. Accordingly, the method relies on the projection of the covariate onto a subspace and maximizes the covariance between its projection and the response conditionally on an extreme event capturing tail information. The covariate and the heavy-tailed response are supposed to be linked through a nonlinear inverse single-index model, and the objective is to infer the index in this regression framework. A new family of estimators is proposed, and its asymptotic consistency with convergence rates under the model is established. Assuming mild conditions on the noise, most of the assumptions are stated in terms of regular variation, unlike those commonly imposed for SIR and single-index regression. In addition, the theoretical analysis is expanded to include a model-free consistency result in probability for the empirical tail-moments in a general separable Hilbert space. Finally, the results are illustrated through a finite-sample study with synthetic functional data and high-frequency financial data, highlighting the effectiveness of the dimension reduction in capturing tail dependence and supporting extreme risk management.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Girard, Cambyse Pakzad

item.title: Phase transition for conditional covariance matrices estimated by importance sampling, and implications for cross-entropy schemes in high dimension
item.description: arXiv:2511.11351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent high-dimensional reliability algorithms, we study a random matrix model corresponding to the estimation by importance sampling of $\Sigma_A$, the covariance matrix of a Gaussian vector conditioned by a rare event $A$. For such models, we show that, in contrast to most random matrix models, the minimal sample size to ensure an accurate estimation of $\Sigma_A$ needs to grow superlinearly in the dimension. More precisely, if $n$ is the sample size and $d$ the dimension, we show that the estimation of $\Sigma_A$ is accurate if $n/d \gg L$ and not accurate if $n/d \ll L$ where $L$ is the maximum likelihood ratio. Moreover, we relate the asymptotic behavior of $L$ to $\lambda_1$, the smallest eigenvalue of the auxiliary covariance matrix, which suggests that $L$ (and thus the minimal sample size) will be larger for small values of $\lambda_1$. Numerical experiments confirm that this insight carries over to recent cross-entropy algorithms, with the best performing algorithms being also the ones with the largest smallest eigenvalue. Although backed up by our theoretical result, this result is surprising as these algorithms were not designed to act on the spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Jason Beh, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos

item.title: A High Dimensional Wild Bootstrap Max-Test for Detecting the Presence of Significant Predictors
item.description: arXiv:2604.27813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a block bootstrap max-test for detecting the presence of significant predictors in a high dimensional setting, allowing for weakly dependent and heterogeneous (possibly non-stationary) data. The number of covariates to be screened may be large $p$ $>>$ $n$, and growing at an exponential rate, provided $\ln (p)$ $=$ $o(n^{a})$ for some $a$ $>$ $0$ that depends on memory decay and the growth of higher moments. We study the problem of correlation screening in a high dimensional marginal regression setting, assuming so-called \textit{physical dependence} in a time series setting. We entirely sidestep covariance matrix estimation and adaptive re-sampling by working with a max-statistic over the many computed parameters. Thus we do not need endogenous selection of the most relevant predictor index yielding non-uniform asymptotics, nor do we need a post-estimation Bonferroni correction. The sequence of non-standard approximating distributions arising from the maximum of an increasing number of estimators is easily approximated by a multiplier (wild) block bootstrap. The max-test controls for size well, performs well against various deviations from the null, including very slight deviations with a weak or sparse signal. A numerical experiment is performed and an empirical example with the VIX volatility index is provided.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan B. Hill

item.title: Self-Distillation is Optimal Among Spectral Shrinkage Estimators
item.description: arXiv:2605.17778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-distillation has emerged as a promising technique for improving model performance in modern machine learning systems. We develop the statistical foundations of self-distillation in high-dimensional linear regression by introducing and analyzing a broad class of estimators, namely spectral shrinkage estimators. We consider both spiked and general covariance matrices. For the former, we establish that when the covariance has $s$ distinct spikes, $s$-step self-distillation achieves optimal prediction among spectral shrinkage estimators, outperforming well-known estimators in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, we show that $s$ steps are necessary for optimality: any $(s-k)$-step distilled estimator is strictly suboptimal for $1 \leq k \leq s$. For general covariance matrices, we show that self-distillation approaches the optimal limiting prediction risk among continuous spectral shrinkage estimators as the number of distillation steps increases. We further develop a generalized cross-validation procedure for selecting the distillation parameters from data and establish an asymptotic oracle guarantee for the resulting estimator. We also study a federated approach where multiple data centers share spectral shrinkage estimators and a common server seeks to aggregate them to achieve optimal performance. In this case, we find that the best local rule again takes the form of self-distillation, though it differs from the optimal rule when data are hosted centrally on a single server. Together, our results explain why self-distillation improves predictive performance and provide a broader statistical framework that connects it to classical shrinkage-based methods.
item.dc:creator: Radu Lecoiu, Debarghya Mukherjee, Pragya Sur

item.title: Robust Ensemble Kalman Filtering Under Observation Noise Misspecification
item.description: arXiv:2605.26881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address observation noise misspecification in Bayesian filtering of dynamical systems via generalised Bayesian inference. Mismatch in tail decay between the true data generating process and an assumed observation model, often indicated via outliers, can strongly impact Bayesian updates in Kalman filters and their ensemble approximations. Adjusting information processing in the analysis step by employing diffusion score matching achieves robustness while maintaining closed-form Gaussian updates and good uncertainty quantification. We provide theoretical properties of this novel Kalman filter in linear Gaussian state space systems covering conjugacy of the analysis step, robustness, covariance stability, and tuning. We extend the approach to non-linear signal dynamics by adapting ensemble Kalman filter variants. Simulation studies on 2D target tracking and the Lorenz-63 and 40D Lorenz-96 systems highlight a critical trade-off between robustness and stability in filtering.
item.dc:creator: Hans Reimann, Sebastian Reich

item.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis
item.description: arXiv:2607.06089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study binary classification when the two classes are elliptical with a shared radial generator $g$. The log-likelihood ratio is then an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link $\varphi=\log g$. For Gaussian classes $\varphi$ is affine and the rule reduces to quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA); otherwise the Bayes link is not the identity. Instead of fitting this link with a spline smoother, we derive its family from the within-class law of the radius and estimate a finite fractional-power projection. We prove that the link is identifiable from the radius law, that the plug-in estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment conditions, and that the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. For $d\ge2$ and non-nested class parameters, the identity link suffices only for affine (Gaussian) generators. The bridge, GAM membership and the affine direction of this dichotomy are verified in Lean 4. We compare against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), re-implemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget. On two UCI benchmarks the derived link ties with the fitted GAM. On six financial series from three asset classes, with validation that respects temporal dependence, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM: better on CAD/USD and tied on the other five. It beats QDA on the three heaviest-tailed series (oil $[+0.023,+0.069]$, S&P 500 $[+0.039,+0.125]$, JPY/USD $[+0.009,+0.047]$) and ties elsewhere. A rate simulation with a closed-form ground truth reproduces the $\sqrt{n}$ rate and, under covariance heterogeneity, QDA's risk floor against the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The derived link thus matches a tuned GAM without smoothing-parameter selection and improves on QDA where the generator departs from the Gaussian.
item.dc:creator: Serhii Zabolotnii

item.title: A Note on the Cut-Locus-Corrected Fr\'echet Mean Central Limit Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.07956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We record two observations concerning \cite{HLW24}. First, the proof of its Theorem~1 yields the population linearization (13)--(14) at \textit{any critical point} of the Fr\'echet function $F_\mu$, under its remaining geometric and measure-theoretic assumptions; neither \textit{isolation} nor a \textit{nonsingular} Hessian of $F_\mu$ is needed. Second, its Theorem~2 is given a shorter proof by applying the M-estimator theorem \cite[Theorem~5.23, pp.~53--54]{vdV98} to negative squared distance in normal coordinates, as opposed to the Donsker argument used there. We verify the pointwise differentiability, local square-integrable Lipschitz bound, second order expansion of population loss, consistency, and empirical maximization hypotheses. The resulting covariance retains the cut-locus correction. The same argument applies to a measurable selection of \textit{local} sample Fr\'echet minima when the population Hessian is positive definite.
item.dc:creator: Susovan Pal

item.title: Identifying Drift, Diffusion, and Causal Structure from Temporal Snapshots
item.description: arXiv:2410.22729v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are a fundamental tool for modelling dynamic processes, including gene regulatory networks (GRNs), contaminant transport, financial markets, and image generation. However, learning the underlying SDE from data is a challenging task, especially if individual trajectories are not observable. Motivated by burgeoning research in single-cell datasets, we present the first comprehensive approach for jointly identifying the drift and diffusion of an SDE from its temporal marginals. Assuming linear drift and additive diffusion, we show that non-identifiability can only arise if the initial distribution possesses generalized rotational symmetries. We further prove that even if this condition holds, the drift and diffusion can almost always be recovered from the marginals. Additionally, we show that the causal graph of any SDE with additive diffusion can be recovered from the identified SDE parameters. To complement this theory, we adapt entropy-regularized optimal transport to handle anisotropic diffusion and introduce APPEX (Alternating Projection Parameter Estimation from $X_0$), an iterative algorithm designed to estimate the drift, diffusion, and causal graph of an additive noise SDE, solely from temporal marginals, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated data from linear additive noise SDEs.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Guan, Joseph Janssen, Hossein Rahmani, Andrew Warren, Stephen Zhang, Elina Robeva, Geoffrey Schiebinger

item.title: Optimal In-context Adaptivity and Distributional Robustness of Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2510.23254v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study in-context learning problems where a Transformer is pretrained on tasks drawn from a mixture distribution $\pi=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{A}} \lambda_{\alpha} \pi_{\alpha}$, called the pretraining prior, in which each mixture component $\pi_{\alpha}$ is a distribution on tasks of a specific difficulty level indexed by $\alpha$. Our goal is to understand the performance of the pretrained Transformer when evaluated on a different test distribution $\mu$, consisting of tasks of fixed difficulty $\beta\in\mathcal{A}$, and with potential distribution shift relative to $\pi_\beta$, subject to the chi-squared divergence $\chi^2(\mu,\pi_{\beta})$ being at most $\kappa$. In particular, we consider nonparametric regression problems with random smoothness, and multi-index models with both random smoothness and random effective dimension. We prove that a large Transformer pretrained on sufficient data achieves the optimal rate of convergence corresponding to the difficulty level $\beta$, uniformly over test distributions $\mu$ in the chi-squared divergence ball. Thus, the pretrained Transformer is able to achieve faster rates of convergence on easier tasks and is robust to distribution shift at test time. Finally, we prove that even if an estimator had access to the test distribution $\mu$, the convergence rate of its expected risk over $\mu$ could not be faster than that of our pretrained Transformers, thereby providing a more appropriate optimality guarantee than minimax lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Ma, Tengyao Wang, Richard J. Samworth

item.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
item.description: arXiv:2605.23362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over na\"ive uniform allocation.
item.dc:creator: Junghyun Lee, Sanghwa Kim, Yassir Jedra, Alexandre Prouti\`ere, Se-Young Yun

item.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths
item.description: arXiv:2606.09121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_\theta$ and the time-ordered transform $R_\theta$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Robust Model Order Selection via Dithered Differential Step-Down Thresholding
item.description: arXiv:2608.29868v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a dithered differential step-down thresholding (DSDT) algorithm for robust model order selection in stationary noise. Evaluating only exceedance counts over a decreasing threshold grid, the proposed algorithm stops when detecting noise extrema value clustering. We prove that deterministic threshold grids are inconsistent under lowered floor detection thresholds due to threshold grid misalignment error. We bound this error using randomized grid dithering. For arbitrary deterministic shifts, any joint noise distribution, and data-dependent thresholds, we obtain non-asymptotic bounds on the estimation risk and family-wise error rate, establishing DSDT as a universal false alarm suppressor for any single-threshold algorithm. When the scale sequence tends to zero or extremes cluster along the search grid, DSDT achieves asymptotic exact order recovery of separated deterministic components exceeding the noise maximum plus the grid step, even below the minimax threshold or without a detection threshold. Using multiple independent dithers reduces error bounds. We provide convergence and consistency analysis for an arbitrary number of dithers. This analysis establishes asymptotic bounds under extreme value laws and non-asymptotic bounds under nondecreasing hazard rates. The results extend to unseparated deterministic shifts, random shifts, unknown noise scales, and multi-dimensional search grids. We show that DSDT is robust to data quantization.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Kharin
